Super Micro Computer (NASDAQ:SMCI) stock dropped 8% to $35.85 this afternoon, leaving the stock up 22% in 2026. The year-to-date gain still might look healthy, and it raises a simple question for shareholders: take profits in SMCI stock or hold on? Measured against the companies selling the same equipment, the picture turns less flattering.

24/7 Wall St.
SMCI Price Target — 24/7 Wall St.

Checking in on the peers, Dell Technologies (NYSE:DELL) stock has gained 307% in 2026 so far, a run that leaves Super Micro Computer stock far behind a direct artificial intelligence (AI) server rival. Furthermore, Hewlett Packard Enterprise (NYSE:HPE) stock is up 166% over the same stretch, which also puts it well ahead of Super Micro Computer stock. Dell and Hewlett Packard Enterprise compete for many of the same AI server customers that Super Micro Computer serves.

To frame the sector backdrop, the iShares U.S. Technology ETF (NYSEARCA:IYW) has gained 30% in 2026, putting it ahead of Super Micro Computer stock as well. Additionally, the broader Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ) is up 19% in 2026, making the NASDAQ 100 tracker the lone comparable here that Super Micro Computer stock has outpaced.

Contractor Plea Puts Super Micro's Supply Chain in Focus

A contractor working with Super Micro Computer pleaded guilty on October 10 in a scheme to divert AI servers containing NVIDIA (NASDAQ:NVDA) chips to China, Reuters reported. The case reaches the company's supply chain through an outside contractor, and the slide in Super Micro Computer stock follows that report. Any link between AI hardware and China tends to draw heavy scrutiny across the server group.

title: Stocks Mostly Up Pre-Bell Ahead of Consumer Inflation Report, More Bank Earnings
detail:
PREMIUM
Stocks Mostly Up Pre-Bell Ahead of Consumer Inflation Report, More Bank Earnings
MT Newswires

^DJI
^GSPC
^NDX
stock board prices market trading equities wall street -Shutterstock

The main US stock measures were mostly tracking in the green in Wednesday's premarket activity as traders await a key consumer inflation report and more major bank earnings.

The S&P 500 rose 0.2%, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average added 0.4% before the opening bell, while the Nasdaq 100 edged down 0.1%. Wall Street finished Tuesday trading lower, with the Dow snapping a three-day winning streak.

The consumer price index report for September is scheduled to be released at 8:30 am ET. Data are expected to show that consumer inflation increased 0.6% sequentially and 3.6% annually, according to a Bloomberg-compiled consensus.

Wall Street projects core CPI, which excludes volatile items such as food and energy, to rise 0.2% month over month and 2.5% year over year for September.

Treasury yields trended down early Wednesday, with the two-year rate retreating 1.9 basis points to 4.77% and the 10-year rate down 2.3 basis points to 5.19%.

Banking heavyweights Bank of America (BAC) and Morgan Stanley are expected to release their latest financial results before the bell, along with BlackRock (BLK), Progressive (PGR), Fastenal (FAST) and State Street (STT).

On Tuesday, JPMorgan Chase (JPM) reported weaker-than-expected third-quarter results, while Wells Fargo's (WFC) revenue fell short of market estimates. Goldman Sachs (GS) and Citigroup (C) topped Wall Street projections.

Shares of Bank of America were down 1.3% pre-bell after the US Treasury Department fined the lender more than $1.21 billion over violations of anti-money laundering and sanctions laws. Liquidia (LQDA) surged 52% after it reached a settlement with United Therapeutics (UTHR) to resolve all pending litigation between the companies.

ASML's (ASML) US-listed stock nudged up 0.3% after the Dutch chip equipment maker reported its latest quarterly results.

Wednesday's economic calendar also has the weekly mortgage applications bulletin, followed by the Federal Reserve's Beige Book, a compilation of economic and business reports from the 12 regional Fed branches.

Fed Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman is slated to speak at 5:40 am ET and later at 10:55 pm. Richmond Fed President Thomas Barkin's remarks are also due on Wednesday.

West Texas Intermediate crude oil inclined 0.6% to $94.69 a barrel, while Brent ticked up 0.1% to $105.81.

The International Energy Agency projects global oil demand to fall by 2.5 million barrels a day year over year in the fourth quarter and 2.6 million barrels per day on average this year, it said in its October monthly oil market report released Wednesday.

"As the Iran war manifests itself through restricted product availability, soaring fuel prices and a deteriorating economic outlook, diesel will register 25% of the drop," according to the agency.

Tensions between Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthi militants continued to escalate, with the Kingdom's energy ministry saying an administrative building belonging to Saudi Aramco was attacked overnight, CNBC reported.

Spot gold dipped 0.3% to $4,165 per troy ounce, while bitcoin was up slightly at $83,152.

U.S. stock futures are trending higher early Wednesday as Wall Street digests incoming inflation data, a massive slate of corporate earnings, and evolving geopolitical risks impacting global energy markets.

The Polymarket traders, a Polygon (CRYPTO: POL) based prediction platform, are leaning bullish for the Oct. 14 trading session. The "S&P 500 (SPX) Up or Down on October 14?" contract currently reflects a 69% chance of a higher open.

Why That Number Matters

Traders are balancing positive equity futures against a critical inflation report and a busy earnings calendar:

Positive Index Futures: Equity futures are pointing to a green open across major benchmarks. Nasdaq 100 futures rose 0.27%, and Russell 2000 futures ticked up 0.26%. S&P 500 futures advanced 0.22%, while Dow Jones futures gained 0.16%.

Crucial Inflation Data & Earnings: Wednesday's economic docket is headlined by September's Consumer Price Index (CPI), core CPI, and annual CPI metrics at 8:30 a.m. ET, followed by the Federal Reserve's Beige Book at 2:00 p.m. ET. A heavy earnings calendar features reports from ASML Holding NV (NASDAQ:ASML), Bank of America Corp. (NYSE:BAC), Morgan Stanley (NYSE:MS), BlackRock Inc. (NYSE:BLK), and Progressive Corp. (NYSE:PGR).

Geopolitics & Oil: Iran is reportedly altering its tactics in the Strait of Hormuz, increasing attacks on shipping vessels to purposefully keep global oil prices elevated ahead of the U.S. midterms. The strategy aims to frustrate U.S. and allied efforts to lower global energy costs. Consequently, crude prices continued to climb; Brent crude rose 0.53% to $106.25 a barrel, and WTI crude gained 0.54% to $94.65 a barrel.

The Bull Case and Market Outlook

Despite concerns regarding rising competition from Chinese chipmakers like ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT), tech strategist Luke Lango argues that not all memory exposure carries the same risk.

While China is catching up in commodity DRAM, high-bandwidth memory (HBM)—the critical component stacked next to AI accelerators—is much harder to produce, leaving Micron's HBM4 capacity sold out through 2027.

View more earnings on SPY

Additionally, Lango notes that chip-export windfalls in South Korea and Taiwan are increasingly being recycled into U.S. stocks and AI names. Unlike the 2008 financial crisis, the current tech boom is backed by real hyperscaler purchases supported by $2.3 trillion in cloud commitments and substantially lower corporate leverage. Lango views this underlying fundamental strength as a solid foundation for tech equities despite short-term volatility.

Investing.com -- Asian stocks mostly fell on Wednesday as an early rebound in artificial intelligence-linked shares lost momentum, while elevated oil prices and caution ahead of U.S. inflation data kept investors on edge.

China's mainland markets led the declines, with the Shanghai Shenzhen CSI 300 falling 1.4% and the Shanghai Composite slipping 0.9%. Australia's S&P/ASX 200 lost 0.6%, South Korea's KOSPI fell 0.4% and Hong Kong's Hang Seng declined 0.1%. Japan's Nikkei 225 edged up 0.1%, while India's Nifty 50 fell 0.4%.

Chinese stocks fell despite stronger-than-expected trade data, as subdued consumer inflation pointed to lingering weakness in domestic demand and accelerating producer prices added to cost pressures.

Wall Street ended slightly lower overnight after mixed bank earnings, although U.S. futures were little changed to higher in Asian trade. S&P 500 futures gained 0.15%, while Nasdaq 100 futures were broadly flat.

Oil prices climbed as attacks around the Strait of Hormuz and renewed strikes on Saudi Arabia raised supply concerns, with Brent near $106.50 a barrel and WTI at $94.40, adding to inflation worries ahead of U.S. CPI data.

Headline inflation is expected to accelerate to 3.6% year-on-year, with a 0.6% monthly increase following August's 0.4% rise, while core CPI is forecast to climb 0.2% month-on-month.

Chipmakers rebound after Tuesday's AI selloff

South Korean chipmakers led the recovery, with Samsung Electronics rising 2.8% and SK Hynix gaining 2% after plunging in the previous session amid growing concerns over Chinese competition. Japan's Kioxia fell 1.8%, while Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing gained 1.4%, Foxconn rose 2.6% and Largan slipped 3.9%.

The previous session's selloff reflected fears that Chinese memory-chip maker ChangXin Memory Technologies is narrowing the technology gap with established manufacturers.

Investors are now looking to U.S. corporate earnings for evidence that technology companies can justify their AI investments. The reporting season began with results from major banks including JPMorgan Chase, Goldman Sachs, Citigroup and Wells Fargo, while Bank of America and Morgan Stanley are due to report later on Wednesday.

Stock indexes settled lower on Tuesday, with the Nasdaq 100 falling to a 1.5-week low. Weakness in chipmakers weighed on the broader market Tuesday amid concerns that investment in artificial intelligence may be unsustainable due to safety concerns and signs of funding strain. Also, a selloff in South Korea's Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix knocked South Korea's Kospi Index down more than -5% on Tuesday to a 2.5-month low amid concerns over intensifying competition from China, adding additional pressure to chip stocks.

However, stocks recovered from their worst levels on Tuesday as bond yields fell on dovish Fed comments that bolstered speculation the Fed won't be forced to raise interest rates aggressively. Fed Governor Christopher Waller said the recent surge in long-term bond yields is helping to curb demand in interest-rate-sensitive sectors, such as housing and automobiles, doing some of the Fed's work to tighten monetary policy. Waller's comments suggest he favors holding policy steady at the FOMC meeting later this month. Also, New York Fed President John Williams said, "It may be appropriate for one more 25 bp Fed rate hike this year, but I don't think at this time I have any reason to believe that we would need to do more."

Hawkish comments on Tuesday from Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee limited the decline in T-note yields when he said inflation tied to the AI boom is "jumping out of its lane" and starting to push up prices in unrelated corners of the economy. The 10-year T-note yield fell -3 bp to 5.21%.

Tuesday's US economic news was supportive for stocks after Sep existing home sales unexpectedly rose +1.5% m/m to 3.99 million, stronger than expectations of a decline to 3.95 million.

Stocks have support from the prospect of solid quarterly earnings results starting this week. Goldman Sachs on Monday raised its three-month view on global equity markets to overweight from neutral, saying. "Earnings growth remains supportive for equities and the recent valuation de-rating has improved asymmetry into the third-quarter earnings season."
